visual: Compact, mound-forming perennial covered in masses of dusky rose-pink daisy-like flowers with golden-yellow centres above narrow mid-green foliage.
water: Keep moderately and consistently moist during active growth, especially while establishing and during prolonged dry spells.
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging. Good airflow helps reduce fungal disease.
prune: Deadhead if desired, then cut stems close to ground level in late autumn. Divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigour.
resilience: Very cold hardy and generally reliable; may be affected by aphids, slugs, snails, eelworm, leaf spot, grey mould or Fusarium wilt.
uses: Front of border, autumn colour, pollinator garden, cottage garden, coastal planting and containers.
uncertain: Frequently sold under the older trade name Aster dumosus 'Rose Crystal'; current taxonomy places Aster dumosus within Symphyotrichum dumosum.

visual: Neat compact perennial forming a rounded mound of green foliage smothered in soft light violet-purple daisy-like flowers with bright yellow centres.
water: Water regularly while establishing and keep moderately moist during active growth; avoid allowing container plants to dry out completely.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained soil; adaptable to most garden soil types.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently waterlogged soil and provide reasonable airflow around dense plants.
prune: Deadhead to keep plants tidy and prolong display, then cut old stems to ground level after flowering or in late autumn.
resilience: Compact and garden hardy; asters can be susceptible to aphids, slugs, snails, eelworm, leaf spots and fungal diseases where airflow is poor.
uses: Patio containers, front of borders, autumn bedding, cottage gardens and pollinator planting.
uncertain: Florensis lists Alpha® Light Purple within its Aster dumosus Alpha® series; modern botanical taxonomy places Aster dumosus within Symphyotrichum dumosum.
No cultivar-specific RHS hardiness rating was located, so H6 follows the RHS rating for Symphyotrichum dumosum.

visual: Compact bushy autumn perennial producing a dense display of vivid fuchsia-pink to purplish-red daisy-like flowers above green foliage.
water: Keep moderately moist while actively growing and during prolonged dry periods, particularly in containers.
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and overcrowding; good airflow helps reduce fungal problems.
prune: Deadhead if desired, then cut stems down to ground level in late autumn. Divide older clumps every few years.
resilience: Cold hardy and valuable for late-season pollinators; may be susceptible to typical aster pests and fungal diseases.
uses: Autumn borders, containers, cottage gardens, wildlife planting and massed seasonal colour.
uncertain: Kientzler lists 'Granat' among its Aster dumosus hybrids and describes it as medium-vigour and garden hardy.
No cultivar-specific RHS profile was located, so cultivation and H6 hardiness use Symphyotrichum dumosum as the baseline.

visual: Upright deciduous blueberry with white bell-shaped spring flowers followed by firm mid- to light-blue berries in late summer and early autumn, with foliage turning orange and red before falling.
water: Keep consistently moist using rainwater where possible, especially during flowering, fruit development and when grown in containers.
soil: Moist but well-drained acidic soil, ideally around pH 4.5–5.5; use peat-free ericaceous compost in containers.
soilWarning: Requires acidic conditions. Alkaline soil or hard-water irrigation can cause iron and manganese deficiency and yellowing foliage.
prune: Once established, prune in late winter by removing dead or weak wood and gradually removing some of the oldest stems at the base to encourage productive new growth.
resilience: Very cold hardy and productive in suitable acidic soil; may suffer vine weevil in containers, root rot in wet soil and nutrient chlorosis where pH is too high.
uses: Edible garden, fruit garden, patio container, raised bed, acid border and wildlife-friendly planting.
uncertain: RHS accepts 'Brigitta' as the cultivar name and lists 'Brigitta Blue' as a synonym.
Best cropping is achieved with another compatible blueberry cultivar nearby for cross-pollination.
